The Deno Slack SDK v2.2.0 now displays an error in your editor when you accidentally register duplicate primary keys for `workflow`, `function`, `datastore`, `customType`, `event` or `provider`.

scope: System notifications now delivered by "Slack" instead of Slackbot

candidates.span: # System notifications now delivered by "Slack" instead of Slackbot

Slack system notifications (such as channel membership changes, User Group updates, Slack Connect alerts, and retention policy notices) are now delivered from the "Slack" system user (`USLACK`) instead of Slackbot.
These notifications are now sent from the new "Slack" system user, `USLACK`.
We renamed the `slack.json` file to `.slack/hooks.json`, and continue to support `slack.json` for existing projects.
There is now a warning shown in `--verbose` output to encourage projects to migrate their `slack.json` to `.slack/hooks.json.`
We've removed the `invalid_app_directory` error from any commands run in nested project directories, and now search for the required `slack.json` file in the project's configuration.
You can now display runtime versions for your application's execution environment using the `doctor` hook.
To enjoy the improved `slack doctor` command experience, existing Deno Slack SDK-based apps must have their `deno-slack-hooks` dependency upgraded to the latest version (`v1.3.0`).
By relying only on the `get-manifest` hook when attempting to get a manifest rather than checking for a `slack.yaml` file, we now surface any errors that are returned when getting the manifest.

The `datastore query` command now supports a `cursor` argument to help you paginate your results the way you want.

scope: The files.upload method is now deprecated

The `uninstall` command is now available from the list displayed when using the `--help` flag.

The `slack create` and `slack init commands` will now detect `pyproject.toml` files, add the `slack-cli-hooks<1.0.0` to the dependency section (when missing), and display instructions on how to install the dependencies.
Python projects now support either or both of the `requirements.txt` and `pyproject.toml` files.
When the `manifest.json` file is changed, the manifest update API is called (`.slack/config.json` must have `manifest.source: "local"`).
We fixed a bug: we now print a debug log if the manifest file was changed but not reinstalled if the `manifest.source` was set to `"remote"`.
We've renamed the `function distribute` command to `function access` (however, the `distribute` subcommand has been added as an alias so you can still use `function distribute`).
We now hide blank `source` errors that may have caused confusion; they have been replaced with more helpful messaging.
We fixed a bug: setting the `source` using the flag for the `slack manifest info` command now takes precedence to project configurations, which are used to determine the default source.

New event: [`app_context_changed`](https://docs.slack.dev/reference/events/app_context_changed.md)**: Slack will send an `app_context_changed` event to your app whenever the user's active context changes.

The `app_context` is now sent to [`message.im`](https://docs.slack.dev/reference/events/message.im.md) and [`app_home_opened`](https://docs.slack.dev/reference/events/app_home_opened.md) events**: Slack will also send the `app_context` to these events if the app is subscribed to the `app_context_changed` event.
We now parse the app manifest fields of `features.search` when gathering an app manifest.
We now automatically set the `SLACK_API_URL` environment variable to the preferred API host used in the auth process.
We now allow `raw_number` cells in [`TableBlock`](https://docs.slack.dev/reference/block-kit/blocks/table-block.md) rows (adds `RawNumberElement`).
We added an optional `action_id` property to the [`WorkflowButton`](https://docs.slack.dev/reference/block-kit/block-elements/workflow-button-element.md) block element.
We replaced the `workspace` command with a new [`app`](https://docs.slack.dev/tools/slack-cli/reference/commands/slack_app.md) command.
We deprecated auth login's `auth` flag in favor of [`token`](https://docs.slack.dev/tools/slack-cli/reference/commands/slack_auth_login.md).
The Slack CLI now supports the `features.agent_view` app manifest property to enable the new _Agent_ experience.

candidates.span: Removes `payment_method_types` as a writable parameter from the [create](https://docs.stripe.com/api/payment_intents/create.md?api-version=2026-09-30.endive), [update](https://docs.stripe.com/api/payment_intents/update.md?api-version=2026-09-30.endive) and [confirm](https://docs.stripe.com/api/payment_intents/confirm.md?api-version=2026-09-30.endive) methods on Payment Intents and from the [create

To migrate, use [Dynamic payment methods](https://docs.stripe.com/payments/payment-methods/dynamic-payment-methods.md) and remove `payment_method_types` and manage available methods from your [payment method settings](https://dashboard.stripe.com/settings/payment_methods).
If you need more control, you can also use `allowed_payment_method_types` to pass a list of types you want to accept, similar to the old `payment_method_types` parameter.
If your integration passes `payment_method_types` when creating, updating or confirming a Payment Intent or Setup Intent, remove it before upgrading to API version `2026-08-26.preview`.

Replace it with [dynamic payment methods](https://docs.stripe.com/payments/payment-methods/dynamic-payment-methods.md) (optionally combined with `excluded_payment_method_types`), or use `allowed_payment_method_types`.
You can now determine if it’s a compliance dispute with the `payment_method_details.card.case_type` parameter.

To contest a Visa compliance dispute, you must acknowledge the network fee by setting the `evidence.enhanced_evidence.visa_compliance.fee_acknowledged` parameter on the [Dispute](https://docs.stripe.com/api/disputes.md?api-version=2025-06-30.basil) to `true` when submitting dispute evidence.
After you acknowledge the fee, the `evidence_details.enhanced_eligibility.visa_compliance.status` value changes to `fee_acknowledged`.

scope: Adds account balance and payout settings with the Balance Settings API
Adds customer parameter to test clock creation

candidates.span: The `customer` parameter accepts an existing customer ID and attaches that customer to the test clock during creation.

scope: Adds the ability to report cancelled payments

candidates.span: You can now create a [Payment Record](https://docs.stripe.com/api/payment-record.md?api-version=2026-09-30.endive) for a cancelled payment in one API call by [reporting a payment](https://docs.stripe.com/api/payment-record/report.md?api-version=2026-09-30.endive) with `outcome` set to `canceled`.

You can no longer create a [price](https://docs.stripe.com/api/prices/object.md?api-version=2025-03-31.basil) with a [usage_type](https://docs.stripe.com/api/prices/object.md?api-version=2025-02-24.acacia#price_object-recurring-usage_type) of `metered` without a specified [meter](https://docs.stripe.com/api/prices/object.md?api-version=2025-02-24.acacia#price_object-recurring-meter).
Using `usage_type` of `metered` without a specified `meter` now returns an error on [Price](https://docs.stripe.com/api/prices/object.md?api-version=2025-03-31.basil) creation.
Removed support for attaching prices of `usage_type=metered` without a set `meter` to Subscriptions, Subscription Schedules and Quotes.

scope: Updates consent modelling for saving cards with Terminal

candidates.span: Removes the `customer_consent_collected` parameter and replaces it with  [allow_redisplay](https://docs.stripe.com/api/terminal/readers/process_setup_intent.md?api-version=2024-09-30.acacia#process_setup_intent-allow_redisplay).
This is a breaking change because it requires `allow_redisplay` when saving card details with Terminal.
For SetupIntents, `customer_consent_collected` has been removed and replaced with `allow_redisplay`.
For PaymentIntents that specify `setup_future_usage`, then `allow_redisplay` must also be passed before collecting card details.
With the new version, you must use `allow_redisplay` to control whether a payment can be shown to a customer again.

scope: Adds support for quantity adjustment to the Customer Portal Configuration API

candidates.span: Now, you can also use the `adjustable_quantity` parameter to programmatically control the quantity that customers can modify on a Customer Portal page for all Customer Portal Configuration objects.

scope: Adds support for Pix recurring payments
Billing Portal Configuration always returns period end date in responses
Adds destination property and new enum values to Reserve Plans, Holds and Releases

candidates.span: [Reserve Plans](https://docs.stripe.com/api/reserve/plan/object.md?api-version=2026-09-30.endive#reserve_plan_object-destination) and [Reserve Holds](https://docs.stripe.com/api/reserve/hold/object.md?api-version=2026-09-30.endive#reserve_hold_object-destination) now include `destination` to indicate where reserved funds are sent.

[Reserve Releases](https://docs.stripe.com/api/reserve/release/object.md?api-version=2026-09-30.endive#reserve_release_object-destination) now include `destination` to indicate where released funds are sent.

scope: Updates schedule customisation for weekly and monthly payouts

candidates.span: We’ve renamed `monthly_anchor` to [monthly_payouts_days](https://docs.stripe.com/api/balance-settings/object.md?api-version=2025-07-30.preview#balance_settings_object-payouts-schedule-monthly_payout_days), which can now configure multiple days of the month for payouts.

We’ve renamed `weekly_anchor` to [weekly_payouts_days](https://docs.stripe.com/api/balance-settings/object.md?api-version=2025-07-30.preview#balance_settings_object-payouts-schedule-weekly_payout_days), which can now configure multiple days of the week for payouts.
The `weekly_anchor` and `monthly_anchor` fields have been replaced with `weekly_payouts_days` and `monthly_payout_days`, respectively.

scope: Replaces SWIFT code with BIC in Financial Addresses

candidates.span: If your code reads `swift_code` from Financial Address responses, it will no longer receive this property.
You must update it to read `bic` instead.
If your code currently reads or sets `swift_code` on Financial Address objects, you must update it to use `bic` instead.

scope: Adds Satispay payments capability to Accounts v2

candidates.span: If your integration uses [Accounts v2](https://docs.stripe.com/api/v2/core/accounts.md?api-version=2026-09-30.endive) and you want to accept Satispay payments, you can now request the `satispay_payments` capability directly on the v2 Account instead of configuring it separately.

scope: Adds additional enum values for Radar manual reviews

candidates.span: If your integration handles the `closed_reason` enum to expect only the previous set of values, this change might break it.

scope: Adds fraud risk assessments to Issuing Authorisations
Makes metadata optional when creating a Batch Job v2

candidates.span: Previously, `metadata` was required, meaning every create request had to include it even if you didn’t need to attach any key-value data to the job.
You no longer need to include `metadata` in every request to create a Batch Job v2.

scope: Adds Link wallet details to Payment Records for card payments

candidates.span: For Link card payments, [payment_method_details](https://docs.stripe.com/api/payment-record/object.md?api-version=2026-09-30.endive#payment_record_object-payment_method_details) now include a [wallet.type](https://docs.stripe.com/api/payment-record/object.md?api-version=2026-09-30.endive#payment_record_object-payment_method_details-card-wallet-type) value of `link`.

If your integration reads wallet details from Payment Records or Payment Attempt Records, [Link card payments](https://docs.stripe.com/payments/link/link-payment-methods.md) may now include a `wallet.type` value of `link` and an optional `wallet.link.funding_source_group` property.

scope: Expands action coverage in Activity Logs
Makes client secret optional for Financial Connections Sessions
Adds the ability to provide proof-of-address documents for connected accounts

candidates.span: Platforms can now use the `proof_of_address` parameter to submit [documents](https://docs.stripe.com/api/accounts/create.md?api-version=2025-06-30.basil) that demonstrate physical presence when they [create](https://docs.stripe.com/api/accounts/create.md?api-version=2025-06-30.basil) or [update](https://docs.stripe.com/api/accounts/update.md?api-version=2025-06-30.basil) accounts.

scope: Makes the radar session property optional in the Payment Evaluations API

candidates.span: This is a breaking change because the `radar_session` property can now return `null` values in API responses, but previously it always contained a value.
If your integration creates payment evaluations and relies on the `radar_session` property always being present, you must update your code to handle cases where this property might be `null`.

scope: Adds Alipay support for invoices and subscriptions that send invoices for collection

candidates.span: If you have existing invoices or subscriptions that should accept Alipay, update `payment_settings.payment_method_types` for the [Invoice](https://docs.stripe.com/api/invoices/update.md?api-version=2026-07-29.dahlia) or [Subscription](https://docs.stripe.com/api/subscriptions/update.md?api-version=2026-07-29.dahlia) object.

scope: Adds time zone support to the Accounts v2 API

candidates.span: Adds the ability to specify a v2 Account’s time zone by adding the optional [timezone](https://docs.stripe.com/api/v2/core/accounts/object.md?api-version=2026-03-25.preview#v2_account_object-defaults-timezone) property to the `defaults` hash.
The `timezone` parameter accepts standard IANA time zone identifiers (such as `America/New_York` or `Europe/London`).

scope: Removes requested field from Accounts v2 capabilities hashes

candidates.span: Removes the `requested` field from the `capabilities` hash, which is used in many parts of [Accounts v2](https://docs.stripe.com/api/v2/core/accounts.md?api-version=2025-12-15.preview).
Instead, you can review the capability’s `status` field, which displays one of the following: `active`, `pending`, `restricted`, or `unsupported`.
If your existing integration relies on the `requested` field, you must update your integration to use the `status` field or rely on the capability being present.
If your integration relies on the `requested` field in the `capabilities` hash in the Accounts v2 API, you must update your code to remove references to this field.
This change improves the succinctness of the API response, as you can still use the `status` field to check the current state of each capability.

scope: Adds Sunbit payments support to Accounts v2

candidates.span: You can now request `sunbit_payments` using the Accounts API v2.
